WorkspaceLock lives on StateStore keyed by run id (state.rs workspace_locks), not on HydratedWorkspace as the row says; the seven sandbox_lease.rs literals are unowned, so this is a justified deviation, but the lead should record it, and S3 must confirm that lock lifetime matches the workspace lifetime.

StateStore::workspace_lock creates a map entry on first call and only take_hydrated_workspace removes it, so a run that never hydrates leaks one Arc per run id, and an in-flight holder of the old lock would be split from a lock created after take; S3 must address both when it wires the calls.

EditError is not the row's closed list: reserved_path, io_error and invalid_argument are added; S3 tool results and the golden strings must use exactly this set, and the row or ledger should be updated to say so.

glob refuses any walk over 5000 entries even under a literal prefix (walk(&base, usize::MAX, WALK_MAX_ENTRIES) then GlobTooBroad), whereas the row says the refusal applies to scans without a literal prefix; a literal-prefixed scan of a large subtree is refused where the row allows it.

On Windows, is_symlink() is false for junctions and other reparse points, so walk, grep and list can descend through a junction that points outside the root; the model cannot create one through these tools, but a hydrated workspace containing one would leak files outside the root.

io_error is never reached by a test, mode preservation on edit (set_permissions on the staging file) has no test, and the attachments/ directory stays readable through read, grep, glob and list because only writes refuse it.

write_atomic renames over the target with no retry, so a Windows sharing violation returns io_error with the original content kept; put's create-only check is not atomic against an external creator, since rename overwrites a file created in the window.

concurrent_edits_from_one_version_serialise_with_exactly_one_winner proves stale-version refusal more than lock behaviour, because each edit is synchronous inside the held write guard and no await point sits in the critical section.
The glob cap test writes 5001 files on every run, which is slow on Windows; a cap parameter or a smaller test seam would keep it fast.

results.notes: Implemented the WS24-S2 pure workspace edit engine in execution-core, plus the run-scoped workspace lock. Deviations from the row, each forced by ownership or the offline cache: (1) `globset` is absent from Cargo.lock and from the local registry cache, so Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are untouched and glob is hand-rolled (`*`, `?`, `**`; no `[...]` classes). The plan's D8 fallback. (2) The lock lives on `StateStore` keyed by run id (`workspace_lock`), not on `HydratedWorkspace`, because seven `HydratedWorkspace { .. }` literals in sandbox_lease.rs are not owned; `take_hydrated_workspace` drops the lock. (3) EditError has three codes beyond the closed list: `reserved_path` (attachments and .verevon* components, refused for writes), `io_error`, and `invalid_argument` (empty old_string, bad regex, bad token, malformed path). (4) `read` refuses files over 1 MiB as too_large. (5) The secret check runs on new_string for edit and on the full content for put. (6) The EOL-normalised and trailing-whitespace ladder steps map spans back to the original bytes; the first replacement drives the diff preview and first_changed_line. Pure functions take no lock; callers hold WorkspaceLock. Test pattern: tests create temp dirs under the OS temp dir and remove them on drop."]
